headline: Computational recovery of usable images from degraded or partial microscopy data
label: Deep Learning Microscopy Image Restoration
summary: Restoration methods for low-SNR, partial, and blurred microscopy data are being benchmarked and extended with new training losses.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational recovery of usable image content from degraded or incomplete microscopy data. A self-referencing three-wave digital holographic microscope reconstruction algorithm recovers whole slide images of cervical smears from partial holograms. A log focal frequency loss is proposed for GAN-based restoration, reporting improved deblurring of nuclei and denoising of zebrafish embryo images. A published benchmark pairs 17,568 high- and low-SNR fluorescence images across 15 sub-datasets and compares five deep denoising models. What is new is the frequency-domain training objective and the direct, paired low-SNR comparison of denoising models. The targets and modalities differ across these items, so the shared element is methodological rather than biological.
